name: flow-chips
title: Wrapping tag chips
summary: Twelve rounded tag chips of different lengths in a flow that wraps them onto as many lines as the width needs.
prompt: A wrapping row of rounded tag chips of different lengths that flows onto new lines.
teaches: Wrap children onto new lines when the row is full with a flow
Make a pill chip from one text: clip roundedRect, a background and inner padding [12, 6]
Space flow items with padding on a wrapper box (end and bottom 8 dp), since a flow ignores spacedBy

snippets.note: a fillMaxWidth flow of twelve chips
one chip: a padding [0, 0, 8, 8] gap box around a clipped, padded text pill

check.describe: Three lines of four chips at width 360; six lines at width 200 (C++ and TypeScript layouts agree). Resized: at 540 wide the chips fill two lines; at 240 wide they need five, more than 140 dp holds, so the root scrolls vertically (verticalScroll) instead of overflowing.

pitfalls: A flow ignores the spacedBy modifier (the Java reference and the C++ player both lay the chips edge to edge); give each item its own gap with padding on a wrapper

Do not fold the gap into the chip as a leading padding ([padding, clip, background, padding]): the Java player treats that first padding as a margin, but the C++ player paints the background over it, so keep the separate wrapper box
The Java layout reference measures text with a stub (100×10), so check line counts with the C++ or TypeScript layout, not java-layout.sh
A flow grows taller as its box narrows: in a fixed-height widget give the container a verticalScroll (or fewer items) or the last lines overflow the document
